Department or Office: Student Activities
Date Open: 10/22/2026
Position available: Available during Term
Description: The Marketing Assistant position for The Cave is responsible for creatively communicating The Cave’s programming across a variety of platforms. The Cave, being both a student organization as well as a venue, provides a variety of programs and services that challenge beliefs, educate others, inspire the individual, entertain the soul, and create a sense of campus community and pride.

Working closely with CSA, SAO, Cave Managers, and staff, the Marketing Assistant will create social media posts, make timely updates to The Cave website, suggest promotional endeavors, and elevate the position of The Cave as a vibrant, exciting all-campus venue. This position plays an integral role in the overall success of The Cave. The Marketing Assistant works approximately 5 hours per week during the academic year.

Marketing Responsibilities
• Regularly post on Instagram about the programs and events occurring in The Cave
• Work with SAO staff to make updates to The Cave’s website
• Create a method of advertising for the website
• Experiment with promotional ideas to encourage new and different campus participation
• Professionally represent the Cave in campus meetings and discussions
• Attend meetings with Cave staff every term and as needed
• Other duties as assigned

How to Apply: Please send a letter of interest and a resume to Cathy Osterman (costerman@) in the Student Activities Office.

Department or Office: Grounds
Date Open: 10/12/2026
Position available: Available during Term and Break
Description: Grounds Student Employee Job Description

Brief Job Description: Grounds Department manages, maintains, and provides installation and improvements of the exterior spaces on campus. These spaces include, but are not limited to, campus grounds, walks, streets, athletic fields, and buffer areas between the campus and Cowling Arboretum.

The Grounds student workers’ duties include: mowing, clearing brush, landscape pruning, spring/fall clean-up, raking, snow removal, help with the set-up/ take-down of the hockey rink, planting of flower beds, and other miscellaneous Grounds duties as assigned.

Qualifications: Positive, energetic attitude; ability to work in outdoor elements: sun, wind, rain, snow; responsible and accountable; and take pride in a job well done.

As a student worker for the Grounds Department, it is mandatory to have a valid driver’s license to operate/drive a UTV as part of the job.

Hours: Working hours are between 7:00 a.m. – 3:30 p.m., Monday-Friday

How to Apply: Please email Grounds Manager: Jon Rabe, jrabe@carleton.edu, if interested to set up an interview.

Department or Office: Reference & Instruction Department, Gould Library
Date Open: 01/04/2027
Position available: Available during Term
Description: The Reference & Instruction Department in Gould Library is hiring 3-4 Peer Research Consultants to work up to ten hours each week. Duties include afternoon, evening, and weekend shifts at the Research/IT desk helping patrons with directional, basic, and more in-depth information questions plus working with librarians to develop and promote Gould’s research services. Peer Research Consultants complete training on topics such as the use of reference sources, library catalog and web pages to support research, databases and indexes, web searching, and research desk and library procedures. Candidates must be second-year Carleton students by the time they begin work as a Peer Research Consultant. Work experience in a library is welcomed but not required.

Essential Job Functions/Responsibilities/Duties:
Assist library patrons at the reference desk
Work 2-3 hour shifts in the evenings during the week and afternoons/evenings on the weekend
Develop and edit online library resource guides
Attend weekly meetings with supervisory team and other Peer Research Consultants
Must be on time for shifts

Supervision Received and Exercised:
A librarian from the Reference and Instruction Department supervises the student in this position. This position has no supervisory duties.

Education/Experience/Skills:
Students in any major are welcome to apply, rising sophomores through rising seniors.
Good communication skills
Customer service experience preferred
Interest in supporting learning among peers
Experience conducting scholarly research preferred
Experience working with technology tools such as Google Drive, Canva, Zotero, PaperCut printing software welcome but not required

Physical demands or Working Environment Requirements:
Work shifts are primarily stationary, sitting at a desk

NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all inclusive. Employees may perform other related duties to meet the ongoing needs of the organization.

How to Apply: Fill out this Google Application form.
You will hear back from supervisors with next steps within one week.

We expect to hold interviews after the application is received. We plan to schedule these interviews for 30 minutes.

If you have any questions, please contact: hchapmantripp@carleton.edu

Job title: TORCH Assistant at Northfield High School

Classification: Student Worker (non-exempt)

Name and address of employer: Carleton College, One North College St, Northfield, MN 55057

Rate of Pay: $13.50 per hour for 2026-2027 academic year

Date Position is Active: Academic Year 2025-2026, September 14, 2026 – June 7, 2027

Department/Office: Center for Community and Civic Engagement

Address of where duties are performed: Northfield High School, 1400 Division St South, Northfield, MN 55057

Supervisor: Tessa Kiesow

Alternate Supervisor: Danielle Trajano, Manager of Student Development Programs       

All Carleton students are eligible to apply.

Objective of the position:

To motivate and guide Northfield students’ academic success through weekly tutoring and mentoring sessions.

TORCH (Tackling Obstacles & Raising College Hopes) works to support and empower Northfield youth in high school and in pursuing future goals, with an intentional focus on partnering with Northfield’s students of color, those from low-income families, and potential first-generation college attendees. The TORCH Program Assistant(s) work directly with TORCH students on academic and social-emotional support. This includes tutoring, offering a listening ear to students facing challenges, helping connect students to resources, serving as a mentor, and helping students understand how their choices in High School can prepare them for success in college and careers.

Duties:

  • Commit to a weekly schedule of working at least two shifts each week at the High School.
  • Build positive relationships with participating students.
  • Assist individual students or small groups with academic needs.
  • Follow up with participating students at least once per week, according to each individual’s needs and progress.
  • Communicate regularly with TORCH staff regarding student progress, emerging needs, etc.
  • Meet all program expectations, including paperwork, background check, data entry tracking student interactions, standards of conduct and attendance policies.

Qualifications:

  • Reliable.
  • Patient.
  • Willingness to get to know high school students, not afraid to start conversations.
  • Desire to motivate and assist students.
  • Effective communication skills.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality.
  • Ability to give and receive instruction.
  • Must pass a criminal background check and complete the required confidentiality agreement before starting work on site.

Hours and Additional Details: 

  • TORCH Assistants are most successful when they spend at least two shifts per week in the TORCH room (for example, Tuesday and Thursday afternoons from 12-3 PM). This allows participating youth to get to know you and feel comfortable working with you. 
  • Hours are only available during the school day. TORCH does not lead afterschool programming on a regular basis. Those needing afterschool hours should inquire about the Middle School Youth Center.
  • Occasionally, TORCH hosts field trips to museums, college visits, outdoor activities, recreational opportunities, etc. that require chaperones and this would be another chance for work study students to gain extra hours.
  • Evaluation will occur at the end of the year.

Transportation to off-campus work site:

Students are responsible for getting themselves to and from their work site, and they are compensated for travel time. Students typically use Campus Go or rent Carleton fleet vehicles for transportation to and from TORCH. 

NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all inclusive. Employee may perform other related duties to meet the ongoing needs of the organization.
